focus.jnote: The surface is still rich, but the floor is shaky. After Tuesday's fresh record, the S&P 500 fell 0.22% Wednesday to ~7,802, the Dow dropped 0.66% and the Russell 2000 slid ~1.3% as the September FOMC minutes confirmed a hawkish lean — most officials expect one more hike by year-end, with no preset path. Three live wires remain: the US–Iran war drags on with Hormuz-shipping risk still elevated and tankers under threat; oil jumped again (WTI ~$90–92, +~5%; Brent ~$102–105) on fresh supply fear and a storm cutting US output; and the 10Y sits near ~5.3%, just off a fresh 24-year high. Gold eased toward ~$4,100 as the dollar firmed (DXY ~102.3). This is a headline-and-rate tape, not one a Sniper sells premium into — and the scanner nearly confirmed it: only one name (PENG) cleared the criteria today, and this time on the bearish side.
focus.notdown: Energy (XLE, XOM, CVX, OXY) carries a war-premium bid and oil jumped ~5% today on renewed Hormuz/tanker risk and a storm cutting US output — but this is a two-sided supply-shock trade, not a clean Sniper. One de-escalation or export-normalization headline and crude gives back premium fast. Megacap tech & AI/semis still lead on a structural story, but that's stretched momentum, not a named catalyst, and any AI wobble gaps the whole index. Watch-only. The only name that cleared validation is PENG — and it boarded bearish.
focus.notup: Rate-sensitive groups (REITs, utilities, housing, small caps) stay pressured with the 10Y near ~5.3% and the minutes keeping a year-end hike in play — the Russell 2000 already fell ~1.3% Wednesday. But selling bear calls into a VIX this low, with a record-adjacent tape that can squeeze shorts on any dovish-data or de-escalation headline, carries its own violent-reversal risk — the disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? Composite ~53 is in WARM and P(≥1% gap) at 38% is above the 35% trigger — either one alone locks out GREEN. More important than the numbers: an active military conflict with oil back toward $90–92 is an unscheduled, open-ended tail, stacked on a bond market at ~5.3% 24-year-high yields and hawkish Fed minutes keeping a year-end hike alive. The scanner boarded only PENG — a Type A post-earnings name whose gap-up faded, now flagged bearish on Grade B+, but on near-zero 0.04x reaction volume. A rich S&P and a low VIX are not a green light when the gap tail is headline- and rate-driven. Stand down on new credit spreads, or push DTE past the headline window and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

setups.read: Penguin Solutions (PENG) reported a clean double-beat Mon 10/6 AMC — EPS beat ~21%, revenue beat ~8%, with a raised FY27 outlook — and it ripped ~13–15% Tuesday to close ~$72.61. The scanner now boards it Type A on the bearish side (Grade B+): the post-earnings pop is fading, with pre-market around ~$70.2, a ~3.3% gap below the prior close. Three honest cautions (voiced here, not by dropping the row per the scanner's hard rules): (1) this is a bearish fade of a fundamentally strong double-beat — an unusual, counter-trend lean; (2) reaction volume is a near-dead 0.04x, far below the 1.3x confirmation bar; and (3) the catalyst is now a few sessions old. Two S/R layers sit just above (gap_floor $72.61 at +3.4%, swing $77.40 at +10.2%). IV is very rich at ~81%. On a RED headline day this is strictly 4-VAL-at-9:35 territory, not a table-pound.

The 0.04x volume is a red flag — half size at most even if it validates, and respect the counter-trend risk of shorting a double-beat. ATM spread ~$0.30 / OI ~5,707 pass the liquidity bar (70.0 strike, 10/16).
